transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Orchid SRE), Maya Patel (Orchid Platform), Liam Chen (Orchid Security), Sam Torres (Orchid Product)

Auto-summary: Discovery on reliability/incident tolerance. Focus on Redwood fallbacks, multi-region routing, SLA expectations for a patient-communication workflow. Action items captured.

Agenda/Topics: fallback policies; multi-region routing; hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs; SLA and monitoring; security/KMS/VPC questions; pilot next steps.

Action items (captured during call): see metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Alex Morgan, account exec at Redwood. with me is Priya, our solutions eng.
[00:12] Priya (SE): hi all, Priya Sharma, I work on runtime and reliability for Redwood. excited to dig into your reliability constraints.
[00:20] Jordan (Orchid SRE): hey Alex, Priya. Jordan here, SRE. we run the patient messaging pipeline and we're evaluating how Redwood fits in. our primary concern is incident tolerance - we need graceful degradation, multi-region failover, and clear SLOs.
[00:35] Maya (Platform): also want to confirm data residency; some customer PHI can't leave region.
[00:42] Alex (AE): totally. quick agenda - we'll do a short set of qualification Qs, then Priya will walk architecture and fallbacks, and then Q&A and next steps. if anything, interrupt.
[00:54] Sam (Product): thanks, we'll jump in.
[01:05] Priya (SE): first qualification: what's your traffic pattern? bursty or steady? what 99p latency matters?
[01:12] Jordan (Orchid SRE): typical is steady during day, peaks during appointment reminders - about 800 rps at peak, 95% sub-200ms, 99p target is 800-1200ms for the whole turnaround including network. availability target is 99.95% for the critical path.
[01:30] Priya (SE): ok good. are you considering hosted or would dedicated/private be required for PHI?
[01:36] Liam (Security): security team prefers Private (VPC) or Dedicated in a single-tenant setup for isolation; hosted could be ok only with strict contractual terms. we also need KMS integration and audit logs.
[01:49] Alex (AE): noted. Redwood supports Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem. we can do KMS and audit logs for both Dedicated and Private. hosted can be used if data residency and policy controls acceptable.
[02:05] Priya (SE): jumping into fallbacks - at a high level Redwood supports model fallbacks (higher-latency/cheaper variations), region routing (primary region with automatic failover), and capacity tiers (hosted, burst to dedicated, etc.). we also do KV/prefix caching to reduce tail.
[02:22] Maya (Platform): can you expand on region failover? if eu-west fails, how do you handle routing to us-east without violating data residency?
[02:34] Priya (SE): good question. we support policy-based routing - you can set allowed failover targets per route. so for PHI traffic you could restrict failover to within EU regions only. if there is no allowable region, Redwood can either queue and retry or return a controlled error depending on your configured SLOs.
[02:55] Jordan (Orchid SRE): so that's policy-level, but what's the detection window? how fast do you detect region-level outage and failover?
[03:03] Priya (SE): detection is a mix of active health checks and real-time metrics. typical detection+switch is in the order of 5-20 seconds depending on conditions; we do gradual rollout to avoid flapping. the failover preserves routing headers and attempts to use compatible model variants in the target region.
[03:23] Sam (Product): what's the visible impact on latency when you fail over across regions?
[03:28] Priya (SE): cross-region adds network RTT, so expect an additional 50-180ms depending on region pair - but if you route to a closer EU region it should be smaller. we also support optional local caching to reduce remote calls for repeated prompts.
[03:45] Liam (Security): about graceful degradation - can Redwood return a degraded response or synthetic fallback if models are unavailable? we can't have blocking failures for patient critical messages.
[03:56] Priya (SE): yes. Redwood supports a layered fallback policy: primary model -> smaller/quantized variant -> cached response -> deterministic template fallback. customers can configure thresholds per-route (e.g., on >1s latency or outage, switch to template). templates can be enriched with last-known-good KV cache values.
[04:16] Jordan (Orchid SRE): that template fallback sounds promising; will it affect audit trail or telemetry? we need to see what was served.
[04:23] Alex (AE): all responses, including template fallbacks, are logged to the audit stream. we can route audit logs to your SIEM and we keep immutable event records for compliance windows.
[04:33] Maya (Platform): what's the SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:38] Alex (AE): Hosted has a general SLA of 99.9% for API availability in our paid tiers; Dedicated includes an SLA of 99.95% (depending on contract) and we have high-availability topologies for Dedicated to help meet that. Private on-prem is more of a support/operational SLA.
[04:55] Liam (Security): how is the HA topology for Dedicated achieved? active-active across AZs?
[05:01] Priya (SE): Dedicated pools can be configured as multi-AZ active-active. for multi-region you can add a second Dedicated pool in a different region with routing policies and automatic failover. we also have cross-pool KV replication for hot cache syncing, though some customers prefer eventual consistency for cache.
[05:18] Jordan (Orchid SRE): cross-pool KV replication - does that replicate PHI? we need to limit where PHI is stored.
[05:24] Priya (SE): KV replication is configurable and can be turned off for sensitive keys. for PHI we recommend keeping KV local to region and using key-level policies to avoid replication.
[05:34] Sam (Product): if we choose hosted for quick start and later move to Dedicated, how seamless is migration?
[05:40] Alex (AE): the API and route config are consistent. you can pin model versions and rollout policies so migrating is usually a config + data migration exercise (KV, keys). Priya can run a migration playbook for your team.
[05:51] Priya (SE): yep, typical steps: baseline workload, run canary on Dedicated pool, verify latencies and regressions, promote. we provide scripts for KV export/import.
[06:02] Jordan (Orchid SRE): about monitoring and observability: we need token-level latency, per-route traces, and alerting hooks to PagerDuty.
[06:11] Priya (SE): Redwood Console exposes token-level cost/latency and per-route dashboards; we've got tracing hooks and webhooks for alerts. we can push events to your monitoring via cloudwatch/logstash or send direct webhooks to your incident system.
[06:26] Liam (Security): KMS integration - do you support customer-managed keys for both Dedicated and Private?
[06:31] Alex (AE): yes, both Dedicated and Private support CMKs (AWS KMS/HSM integrations). Hosted supports envelope encryption with optional BYOK in enterprise contracts.
[06:43] Maya (Platform): encryption in transit and at rest?
[06:46] Priya (SE): TLS in transit by default. at rest we encrypt using KMS-managed keys; in Dedicated you can use your own CMK.
[06:54] Jordan (Orchid SRE): one more Q: performance regression safety. if you roll a new model version and quality drops, can Redwood automatically roll back?
[07:03] Priya (SE): we have rollout features - canary, A/B, automatic fallback to previous version on error rates or latency regressions. quality monitoring is possible via eval hooks you can use to run prompt sets and trigger alerts on regressions.
[07:18] Sam (Product): ok, let's talk numbers - Priya, can you summarize expected 99p latencies for our peak workload on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[07:25] Priya (SE): rough numbers: on Dedicated with the recommended instance types and quantization we typically see 99p ~ 700-900ms for your workload profile; Hosted similar for same instance class but subject to shared tenancy variance - might see occasional spikes. with caching and batching you could reduce cost but batching can increase tail latency so it's a tradeoff.
[07:46] Jordan (Orchid SRE): is there a recommended instance sizing for 800 rps?
[07:50] Priya (SE): we'll dimension Dedicated pools - preliminary estimate: 4-6 GPUs (A100 equivalent) for persistent low-latency, with autoscale headroom for bursts. Priya notes: exact depends on model size and sequence length. we'll do sizing during the bench.
[08:06] Alex (AE): quick sanity: competitor question - any reason you'd choose Anthropic/OpenAI over Redwood?
[08:12] Jordan (Orchid SRE): we've looked at them; main reasons are maturity of inference guarantees and enterprise controls. we like Redwood's routing and private deployment options.
[08:21] Maya (Platform): plus the KV caching and explicit fallback policy is attractive.
[08:26] Priya (SE): good to hear.
[08:30] Alex (AE): wrapping toward next steps - we'll send SOC2 and network diagram, dedicated pricing and sizing, and a bench plan. Priya will run a bench with your sample traffic.
[08:42] Jordan (Orchid SRE): one ask - can you show an example of the fallback logs and how they appear in the audit events? we need to verify for compliance.
[08:51] Priya (SE): yes, we have an audit sample; I'll attach a redacted file. Alex will include it in the follow-up.
[08:57] Sam (Product): timeline - we're aiming to decide by end of month for pilot start in Nov.
[09:03] Alex (AE): that timeline works. we'll aim to get docs and pricing to you by 10/09, bench run scheduled the week of 10/12.
[09:12] Liam (Security): small note - we need a data processing amendment and details on retention periods.
[09:18] Alex (AE): understood. legal will follow up; we'll include DPA and retention defaults, plus options for custom retention.
[09:26] Maya (Platform): just to confirm, if we configure route-level non-failover for PHI, and the region is down, Redwood will either queue or error - but not route to an unauthorized region, correct?
[09:35] Priya (SE): correct, it's policy enforced; you choose queue vs error. queueing preserves order and retries as capacity returns.
[09:41] Jordan (Orchid SRE): any data on real-world detection times you've observed? 5-20s is fine but curious on median.
[09:48] Priya (SE): median detection is ~8-12s in our telemetry for region failures, dependent on network conditions; we can share anonymized metrics.
[09:58] Alex (AE): ok great. final recap: Alex send SOC2 + network diagram + pricing + sample audit logs; Priya run bench and share latency/cost spreadsheet; Orchid provides traffic profile and retention requirements.
[10:10] Jordan (Orchid SRE): thanks all, helpful. we'll get Jordan's sample payload and traffic CSV over.
[10:16] Alex (AE): thanks everyone; we'll follow up with calendar invites for bench kick-off.
[10:22] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional label swaps and minor mis-hearings; speakers sometimes truncated. references: Priya referenced abenchmark spreadsheet (link to bench plan: https://redwood.example/bench/orchid-2026) and audit sample (attached by Alex in follow-up).
